reason: The text demonstrates extensive open expression of views throughout the narrative. Multiple examples show people freely speaking: Abimelech's relatives persuade the people of Shechem; the inhabitants openly discuss and respond to political proposals; Jotham publicly delivers a critical parable to all the people (שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶם - 'Hear me, inhabitants of Shechem'); Gaal son of Ebed openly challenges Abimelech's rule (וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ גַּ֣עַל בֶּן־ עֶ֗בֶד); and the people curse their king (וַֽיְקַלְל֖וּ אֶת־ אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ). The narrative depicts active political discourse, debate, and contested viewpoints rather than suppression or discouragement of speech.
